families.family: Tehran Internet / Online rounds (incl. 2014/2015 per-university 'Iran-Internet-PC-*' rows)

facts.participants: National (Iran-wide) field, med ~394 teams per maintainer CMS; drawn from all major Iranian universities (the onsite regional it feeds had teams from 58 different universities in 2018). Foreign teams may also enter via the same route (fee waived).
facts.problemset: Own fresh problemset each year, prepared by the Sharif/Tehran-site scientific committee; it is a numbered national series ('14th Iran Internet Contest' on 24 Nov 2016, i.e. the series predates the maintainer's 2013+ rows, first edition ~2003). Problemset is distinct from the onsite Tehran regional's set.
facts.qualification: Explicit gate on the WF path: registration for the Tehran onsite regional is a two-step process — step 1 is the Internet Contest ('register your team on the ICPC site under Asia Tehran – Internet Programming Contest'), and 'only teams with at least one problem solved in the Internet Contest are eligible to proceed' to the onsite Tehran regional (75-team site cap, per-institution quotas). Tehran regional advances champions to the ICPC World Finals.
facts.format: Online by definition and for its entire life — it is the 'Internet Contest'; never had an onsite era of its own. In the mid-2010s teams sat the round at proctored university venues; the parent onsite regional is a separate December event at Sharif University of Technology.
facts.host: Sharif University of Technology (ICPC Asia Tehran site committee, icpc.sharif.edu / icpc.ir); judged on the site's own systems.

for: Passes R1: genuinely national multi-university field (~394 teams median, all major Iranian universities).
Passes R2: own annual problemset, own numbered identity ('Nth Iran Internet Contest') distinct from the onsite regional.
Passes R3: hard gate — solving >=1 problem in it is a formal precondition for the Tehran onsite regional, which sends teams to WF.
against: Fails R4 (only R4): it is an online preliminary by construction — exactly the class the 'mainline = not online' rule excludes.

Identity lens on the 2014/2015 'Iran-Internet-PC-Sharif/SBU/AUT/IUST/Shiraz/Fanni/IU' rows: these are best read as proctored SITES of the one simultaneous internet round, not seven contests — same 'Iran-Internet-PC' naming stem, the roster is exactly Iran's major CS schools, the contest is a single numbered national series, and in every other year (incl. today) it is a single CMS row ('Asia Tehran – Internet Programming Contest'). They should be collapsed into one contest per year (part-of-parent of the internet round, which is itself the qualifier of the Tehran regional).
families.confidence: high (family characterization); medium (per-university rows = sites of one round — Iranian hosts icpc.ir/icpc.sharif.edu were unreachable from this environment, so same-date proof of all 2014/2015 site rows could not be pulled; based on naming stem, single numbered series, and single-row structure in all other years)

families.family: Oman sub-region contests (2025-2026: Capital / Coastline / Midland / Southern / Oriental + Seniors row)

facts.participants: ~20-80 teams per sub-region (maintainer CMS); nationally the OCPC system drew 65 teams / 194 contestants from 21 universities and colleges across the governorates in 2025. Each sub-region groups the institutions of several governorates (2025: Muscat governorate = Capital; Sohar for North+South Al Batinah = Coastline; Nizwa for Ad Dakhiliyah + Ash Sharqiyah = Midland; the 2026 rows add Southern (Dhofar/Salalah area) and Oriental (Ash Sharqiyah), splitting the map five ways).
facts.problemset: Not verified who sets the sub-region problemsets or whether the simultaneous sub-region rounds share one problemset (R2 sibling-sharing question is OPEN); the national final is a classic single 5-hour ICPC-style round, one problemset for all teams.
facts.qualification: Sub-region contests qualify teams to the OCPC national final (e.g. OCMT 'Codebreakers qualify for OCPC 2025 Finals'); the OCPC final (Sultan Qaboos University, 8-10 Apr 2025) selected 3 teams 'to represent Oman in the regional contest to be held in the Arab Republic of Egypt' = the ACPC (Africa & Arab Collegiate Programming Championship), which is the ICPC super-regional championship on the WF path (Oman is among the 15 countries at ACPC 2023, Luxor).
facts.format: Onsite events: 2025 was the FIRST year with regional qualifying contests, 'held in Sohar, Nizwa and Muscat' (physical venues); national final onsite at SQU. The 2026-season CMS rows (e.g. 'The 2025 ICPC Oman Capital Sub-region Collegiate Programming Contest', slug OCPCCap-2026) are the second edition with five sub-regions.
facts.host: Organized by Oman's Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology (MTCIT) with academic partner Sultan Qaboos University, the University of Technology and Applied Sciences (UTAS), the Programming Academy, and technical partner OQ; sanctioned rows in the ICPC CMS (icpc.global finder: OCPC, OCPCCap-2026).

for: Passes R1: each sub-region is a multi-university grouping of governorates (21 institutions across the system; UTAS branches, SQU, private universities/colleges), not a single-campus qualifier.
Passes R3: real gate on the WF path — sub-region -> OCPC national final -> 3 Oman teams to ACPC -> ICPC WF chain.
Passes R4: onsite contests at physical venues (Sohar/Nizwa/Muscat 2025; five venues in the 2026 season), unlike the online-preliminary families in this batch.
Own identity: named geographic sub-regions with own venues and CMS rows, below an already-catalogued national final.
against: R2 open: could not verify unique problemsets per sub-region — if the five sub-region rounds run simultaneously on one shared problemset, they are siblings sharing a set (flag, per maintainer's R2 note), or arguably five sites of one qualifier.
Structure is brand new (first edition April 2025) — little track record; row naming/season mapping (April-2025 events vs '2026' rows) needs one-time reconciliation in the CMS.

The 'Seniors' row: no press or CMS evidence found of what it is; MTCIT's description of OCPC 2025 covers collegiate teams only. If it is a graduates/professionals division it gates nothing on the WF path (fails R3) and should not be mainline.

facts.participants: India-wide online fields up to ~3000 teams (maintainer CMS); teams compete remotely 'generally from their respective colleges'; onsite Amritapuri capacity 230 teams (220 general + 10 women-only slots, 2024 rules); Rs.1500/team fee (2026 season).
facts.problemset: Own fresh problemsets (CodeChef-/CodeDrills-hosted with credited setters), distinct from the onsite regionals' sets. In unified years there is literally ONE shared online contest whose single problemset serves multiple sibling regionals, each drawing its own rank list.
facts.qualification: Gates the onsite Indian regional(s) (WF path): 'Selection is based on performance in the preliminary round and the applicable ICPC regional selection rules' — rank-based advancement with per-institution caps (max 4/college in top-15 phase, K<=4 overall, min-solve threshold N).
facts.format: Online every year by design. Sharing timeline: separate per-regional online rounds ~2012-2017 (Amritapuri's round on CodeChef from 2012); ONE common online round for all India regionals 2018-19 and 2019-20 (CodeChef); 2020-21 COVID cycle — the Amritapuri REGIONAL itself was held online (preliminary 16 May 2021, 'regional' 30 May 2021); 2021-22 and 2022-23 — only 2 regionals ran, each with its own separate qualifier (CodeDrills era); 2023-24 — 'Amritapuri First Round' online contest (own row, finder slug Asia-Amritapuri-First-Round-2024); 2024-25 — 'a single Preliminary Online Contest for all three Regional Sites in India (Kanpur, Amritapuri, and Chennai)' (16 Nov 2024) with a separate rank list per site; 2026-27 — 'ICPC India Preliminary Online contest' 3 Oct 2026 feeding the Amritapuri onsite (itself multi-venue: Kollam/Bengaluru/Coimbatore/Mysuru, 1-2 Jan 2027, same problems at all venues).
facts.host: Amrita (Amritapuri site committee, amritaicpc.in) with platform partners CodeChef (2012-2020), CodeDrills (2021-2023), later seasons again CodeChef/CodeDrills; the unified rounds are run jointly for the participating regional sites.

for: Passes R1: the largest multi-university field in India (~3000 teams).
Passes R2 with a caveat to note: fresh problems, but in 2018-2020 and 2024+ one contest's problemset is SHARED across 2-3 sibling regionals (one contest, multiple parents' rank lists).
Passes R3: sole gate into the Indian onsite regionals -> WF.
against: Fails R4 (only R4): online preliminary by design; name and identity are purely functional ('India Preliminary Online', 'First Round') under the parent regionals' geography — machinery of the parents.

families.family: 'Asia Regionals Online Contest I/II' (2026 CMS rows) + 'Asia Jakarta New Online Contest' (2014)

facts.participants: Asia Regionals Online Contest (I)/(II): thousands of teams from hundreds of mainland-Chinese (+ Hong Kong) universities; despite the pan-Asia name it is the ICPC Asia EAST CONTINENT (China) online preliminary series (Chinese: 网络预选赛). Jakarta 2014 online contest: 307 teams across Indonesia.
facts.problemset: Fresh problemsets per round (two independent rounds, I and II, each its own set) on the PTA/Pintia judge; boards archived by XCPCIO (e.g. 'The 49th ICPC Asia Regionals Online Contest (II)'). Jakarta 2014: own national qualifier set (report: 'National Preparation Contest').
facts.qualification: China: results are 'an important reference condition for advancing to the regional sites' — the 2024 notice names Chengdu, Nanjing, Hangzhou, Shanghai, Shenyang, Kunming, Hong Kong, Xi'an; universities wanting onsite Asia-regional slots must enter; the chain continues onsite regionals -> Asia-EC Final (quota allocation published by the same HQ) -> WF. Jakarta 2014: top 50 of the national online contest got a free pass to the Asia Jakarta onsite regional; identity-wise it is the ancestor of today's 'Jakarta - Indonesia National Contest' rows (finder slugs Jakarta-National-2025/2026).
facts.format: Online. China: two 5-hour online rounds each September (2024: Sept 15 and Sept 21; 2025 edition = the '2026' CMS rows, registration notices Aug 2025), CNY 100/team/round, on PTA (pintia.cn); series in this unified form since ~2020/2021 (PTA archive from 2021), successor of the per-regional Chinese online preliminaries of 2015-2019. Jakarta 2014: one national online round (9 Nov 2014); the 'New' in the CMS name is not explained by the official regional report (possibly a re-run; unresolved).
facts.host: China: ICPC Asia-EC Online Preliminary Organizing Committee under ICPC Beijing headquarters at Peking University (icpc.pku.edu.cn), platform PTA/Pintia. Jakarta 2014: BINUS University (Asia Jakarta regional host).

for: Passes R1: broadest multi-university events in the archive (all Chinese ICPC universities; all Indonesia respectively).
Passes R2: own fresh problemsets (I and II are two distinct contests, not one contest at two sites).

Passes R3: hard gate — Chinese universities' slots at ALL mainland (+HK) onsite Asia regionals flow from these results; the regionals feed EC Final and WF. Jakarta 2014 online gated free passes into the Jakarta onsite regional.
against: Fails R4 (only R4): both are online preliminaries; that is their entire identity.
Naming trap: 'Asia Regionals Online Contest' is NOT a pan-Asia round — it gates only the East-Continent (China) regional system; catalogue it under Asia-EC, not as an Asia-wide round.

Identity lens: the Jakarta 2014 online contest has its parent's geography (Indonesia national qualifier of the Jakarta regional) and a purely functional name — part of the parent's machinery; its modern descendant already exists as the 'Indonesia National Contest' rows.

notes: R4 split requested by maintainer: families failing ONLY R4 (online) and passing R1-R3 = Tehran Internet rounds, Dhaka online preliminaries, Amritapuri/India online preliminaries, and the Chinese 'Asia Regionals Online Contest I/II' (+ Jakarta 2014 online). None of them fails R1 (all are mass multi-university), none fails R2 outright (all have fresh problemsets, with SHARING caveats: India's unified rounds 2018-2020 and 2024+ are one contest shared by 2-3 sibling regionals; Oman sub-regions' sharing unknown), and all satisfy R3 (each is a hard gate on a WF-path onsite contest). Oman sub-regions are the only family in this batch that PASSES R4 (onsite).

Identity-lens collapses recommended: (a) 2014/2015 'Iran-Internet-PC-<University>' rows -> sites of the single annual Iran Internet Contest (one contest/year); (b) 'Asia Jakarta New Online Contest 2014' -> Indonesia national online qualifier of the Jakarta regional (ancestor of the 'Jakarta - Indonesia National Contest' rows); (c) Dhaka/India preliminary rows carry their parents' geography and functional names — registry entries linked to parents, not standalone mainline contests.

False leads to avoid: ocpc.camp is 'OCPC LLC, Dover, Delaware' — a training-camp business, NOT Oman's OCPC; TUM's 'Amirkabir 2015' history entry (57 teams, Tehran+Munich, 20 Nov 2015) is AUT's separate open contest, not the Iran-Internet-PC-AUT row.

Unresolved/needs-info: (1) Oman 'Seniors' row — no press/CMS evidence found; MTCIT describes the collegiate contest only; if a graduates/professionals division it fails R3 -> keep out of mainline (registry) until OCPC clarifies. (2) Whether Oman's five sub-region rounds share one problemset. (3) Tehran regional's COVID-year (2020/2021) format — Iranian hosts (icpc.ir, icpc.sharif.edu/.ir) were unreachable from this environment (timeouts), so unverified; does not affect the internet-round family's verdict. (4) Dhaka preliminary rows before 2017 (any 2015/2016 prelim) unverified. (5) Jakarta 2014: why the CMS row says 'New' Online Contest (official report calls it 'National Preparation Contest', 9 Nov 2014) — possibly a re-run; unresolved.
